answer.rationale: Finance mandate requires an 18% spend cut; the low-cost vendor's quote meets it alone. memory_c2 documents that the same vendor cut unit cost sharply last year with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing, supporting the switch. Contract expires in 14 days, so deferring or renewing risks missing the mandate; negotiating on the incumbent likely cannot match the vendor's price. Operating at 94% of committed volume without buffer argues against adding a second source this cycle (split volume raises delivery risk). Switching directly to the incumbent-locked vendor is the lowest-TCO path while the prior record reduces delivery and onboarding risk.
